notes.meaning: Paul urges believers, in light of God's great mercy, to offer their whole lives and bodies to Him. Unlike the animal offerings of the past, this is a living, holy sacrifice that truly pleases God. Dedicating oneself to God in this way is the sensible and proper way for a Christian to worship.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic teaching views the Mass as an unbloody sacrifice of Christ for sins, while Protestants understand this verse to teach that animal sacrifices are finished and Christians now offer spiritual sacrifices of their own lives.

notes.meaning: Believers are warned not to let the patterns and sinful habits of the present world shape their lives. Instead, God transforms Christians from the inside out by making their minds new. A renewed mind allows a person to recognize and gladly follow God's good, pleasing, and perfect plan.

Speaking with apostolic authority, Paul cautions every believer against the danger of pride. No one should think too highly of their own importance or abilities. Instead, each person should view themselves with clear, honest judgment, based on the trust and gifts God has given them.

Just as a human physical body is made of many parts that each have different jobs, believers together make up one body in Christ. Although Christians have diverse roles, they belong to one another and rely on each other to function well.

God gives different gifts to His people through His grace, so believers should use whatever ability they have received. If someone is given the gift of prophecy to declare God's message, they must speak in proper agreement with their faith.

differ.view: Christians in this tradition understand the proportion of faith to mean that all preaching and prophesying must strictly agree with the standard of biblical doctrine.
Many evangelicals believe this phrase means that the speaker must share God's message only up to the level of personal trust and conviction God has given them.

notes.meaning: Those who have received the gift of practical service should dedicate themselves to serving others faithfully. Likewise, those who are gifted to teach should focus on explaining God's truth clearly.

Those whose gift is encouraging should give their energy to lifting others up in faith. Those who share their resources must do so generously and without selfish motives, leaders must guide people with earnest diligence, and those helping the hurting should do so with a cheerful heart.
Christian love must be completely sincere and without any hypocrisy or fake show. Believers must actively detest what is sinful and evil, while holding tightly to whatever is good and right.

Christians are called to treat one another with the warm, devoted affection found in a loving family. Instead of seeking attention or praise for themselves, believers should eagerly take the lead in showing honor to their brothers and sisters.
Believers should never grow lazy or sluggish in doing the work of God. Instead, they must keep an eager, burning enthusiasm in their spirits as they faithfully serve the Lord Jesus.

Believers can stay joyful because of the confident hope they have in God's eternal promises. That firm hope gives them strength to bear trials patiently, and steady, persistent prayer keeps their faith strong.
Christians must readily share their money and goods with fellow believers who are in need. They should also actively look for opportunities to welcome travelers and strangers into their homes.
When people mistreat or persecute believers, Christians must respond by asking God to bless them. Believers are forbidden from wishing harm or calling down curses on their enemies.

Followers of Christ are called to enter warmly into the joys and sorrows of those around them. When others experience blessings, believers should rejoice with them without jealousy, and when others suffer, believers should weep with them in comfort.

Believers should strive to live in harmony and mutual understanding with one another. Rather than chasing high status or social pride, Christians ought to enjoy the company of ordinary people and humble tasks, avoiding the trap of conceit.

No Christian should ever pay back an injury or insult with another wrong. Instead, believers should think carefully beforehand about doing what is visibly honest and honorable in the sight of all people.

Christians must do everything within their own power to maintain peaceful relationships with everyone. While other people may sometimes refuse peace, believers should ensure that no quarrel begins or continues through their own fault.

Believers must never take personal revenge when someone wrongs them. Instead, they should step aside and leave justice in the hands of God, who has promised in Scripture that vengeance belongs to Him alone.

Instead of hurting an enemy, believers must meet his practical needs by giving him food and drink. Responding to hostility with genuine kindness often brings a burning sense of shame and sorrow that can lead an enemy to repentance.

other.label: Popular modern teaching
other.view: A popular modern explanation suggests this phrase refers to an ancient custom of carrying a pan of coals on the head to share fire with a neighbor, making the act purely an expression of warmth and aid.

notes.meaning: Believers must not allow the wrongs done against them to break their spirit or drag them into bitterness and revenge. Instead, Christians win the true victory by answering hostility with persistent goodness, kindness, and patience.
